sentences: The detective (an actor) pretends to be an enemy spy to aid the scientist (another actor) and his new invention, a bombsight, in escaping a secret police trap in a foreign country.
The detective and the scientist fly to the capital, where the detective places him under the protection of his friend, the doctor (a third actor).
The scientist slips away against the detective's instructions for a secret reunion with his fiancée (an actress), and gives her an envelope containing a coded message.
He tells the fiancée to give it to the detective if anything should happen to him.
The German spies' attempt to abduct the scientist as he leaves the fiancée's apartment is foiled by a passing local bobby.
The scientist successfully demonstrates the bombsight for the official (a fourth actor) and observers from the bomber force's command.

The scientist, now under the protection of the inspector (a fifth actor) and the police force, tells the official that although willing to provide the British with his bombsight, only he will know its secret and has a complex plan for its manufacture to keep the secret safe.
He separates his invention into four parts and gives one to each of four Swiss scientists, known only to him and not to each other, to construct separately.
Soon after, the detective receives a call from the inspector telling him that the scientist has disappeared.
The detective goes to the fiancée's flat, where he receives the scientist's envelope.
Rather than the coded message, the message inside is from the detective's nemesis, the master criminal (a sixth actor), who is now working for the Germans.
Disguising himself as a former associate, one of the master criminal's old henchmen, the detective searches a district of the capital for information.
He encounters two henchmen the one-legged man (a seventh actor) and the other henchman (an eighth actor), but is captured by the master criminal.
The detective is put into the false bottom of a sea chest, but is rescued when the doctor and the inspector observe the henchmen struggling with its unusual weight.
The detective returns to the fiancée's flat to search for clues to the message's contents.
He finds impressions of the message left on a notepad page by immersing it in "fluorescent salts... and then photograph(ing) it by ultraviolet light."

The detective breaks the first three lines of a cunningly modified substitution cipher, which are the identities and locations of three of the scientists, but cannot break the fourth line, which has been altered as an added precaution.
He soon learns that the master criminal has murdered all three scientists and stolen their parts.
Meanwhile, the master criminal, also unable to break the fourth line, tortures the scientist for the name of the fourth scientist.
The detective deduces the change in the code and breaks the fourth line, identifying the scientist as the professor (a ninth actor).
The master criminal accidentally deciphers the code.
He sends agents to abduct the professor, who has the brilliance to put the four parts together should the scientist not recover from torture.
The German agents bring the scientist, who is actually the detective in disguise again, to the master criminal's seemingly undetectable stronghold.
Unknown to the master criminal, the detective had the real professor attach an apparatus to their car that drips luminous paint (which the doctor helped prepare) at regular intervals.
To stall for time, the detective uses the master criminal's vanity and pride to trick him into slowly bleeding the detective to death "drop by drop".
The detective is saved at the last minute by the doctor and the inspector, who with the professor's help, successfully followed the luminous paint trail.
The police force apprehends the spies, but the master criminal escapes.
When he attempts to complete his escape through a secret passageway, he falls 60 feet to his death; the detective has discovered the criminal's hidden trap door and left it open.
With the scientist saved and the bombsight recovered, the doctor notes that things "are looking up... this little island is still on the map".

The detective is called into the "council" of the British intelligence service by the official, to assist in stopping enemy saboteurs operating in the country, whose activities are announced in advance in radio broadcasts by "the broadcaster".
The agent, one of the detective's operatives, is killed with a German dagger in his back.
Before he dies, the agent utters a single name.
Later, the detective and the doctor go to a dockside district of the city, where they meet with the agent's wife.

The detective tells the council that, through the use of an oscilloscope to carefully analyze and compare sound wave patterns from radio broadcasts of live vs. pre-recorded voices, he has determined that "the broadcaster" is actually recorded on phonograph records in the country, but broadcast from the enemy country.
Using a tip from the wife, the detective and the doctor go to the old docks of that name, where they are followed by the other official of the council.

The three men are captured by a group of enemy spies led by the spy leader however the detective, the doctor and the other official are freed by some of the local men as they attack the enemy spies, although the spy leader manages to escape through a trap door to a waiting speedboat.
The wife pretends to be a thief on the run and joins the spy leader.
She finds out that the spy leader plans to go to the official's country estate in a nearby county that night.

There the detective and the official watch a German plane land and although the official fires at it, the spy leader has time to pas a package to the pilot who then successfully takes off while the spy leader has time to hide.
After one of the detective's informants traces the spy leader and the wife to the south coast of the country, the detective forces the council to go there with him.
With the support of British troopers, the detective captures the spy leader and a group of German soldiers stationed in an abandoned church.
There he reveals the true identity of "the broadcaster" as the official, who happens to be an impostor.

The detective then reveals that in World War I, the real official was a prisoner in a German war camp and had an uncanny resemblance to a certain German agent, a member of the German secret service; one day the real official was taken out and executed; the gentleman who called the detective into the case was the German agent himself who had been posing as the official for 24 years; the detective then adds that the official had no immediate family, so his private life was well studied by the German agent, who also studied at a famous university and had knowledge of English language and manners.
So, with a little help of plastic surgery, not to mention the resemblance to the official in the first place, the deception was carried out thoroughly.

The detective also concludes that the real official carried a scar from childhood, the one the German agent carried from plastic surgery was approximately 20 years old – the clue that gave away the fact that he was an impostor.
The detective then informs the spies that the German invasion force has been destroyed.
The angry spy leader shoots and fatally wounds the wife, but is killed himself as he attempts to escape.
The council stand around the murdered wife and swear that her heroic death will not be in vain.
The doctor is working as resident physician at the family manor in a northern county, a stately home which is also used as a hospital for a number of servicemen suffering from shell shock.

When the sister displays her feelings for one of the wounded American fighter pilots, the captain, who is currently recovering at the family estate, her brothers, the elder brother and the younger brother, are quick to show their dismay.
One of the physicians working at the estate, the other physician, is assaulted by an unknown assailant when out on a walk.
The doctor, who is in charge of the medical facility, goes to fetch his dear friend the detective to bring some clarity to the case of the attack.
Upon his arrival at the estate, the detective discovers the dead body of one of the brothers, the elder brother.
The inspector of the police force is put on the case to solve the murder and immediately arrests the American captain as a suspect.
The detective is of another opinion about the flyer's guilt and continues to investigate on his own.
The younger brother is formally made the new head of the estate the next day with the aid of his sister.
But after only one day of running the estate, the younger brother, too, is found murdered, lying in the trunk of the car.
The inspector suspects the family butler to be the murderer because the younger brother had just fired him.
Trying to arrest the butler, the inspector becomes lost in the manor's secret passageways.
Meanwhile, the detective and the doctor look into the special "family ritual" that the family uses to appoint the new head of the family.
They find the words used in the ritual hidden in the sister's room and try to copy the ritual, which involves replaying a giant chess game on the checkered floor of the house's main hall.
As pieces in the game they use the household staff and servicemen.
The game gives them clues to the family's secret burial crypt underneath the house, and there they find the butler murdered, clutching a case containing an old document.
The detective examines the body for clues and sets a trap for the murderer.
After the others have retired for the night, the detective sneaks back into the crypt and waits for the murderer to reappear.
Before long, the other physician appears, and the detective confronts him with the evidence that he has found and observed throughout the investigation.
The other physician, however, manages to overpower the detective and takes his revolver.
The other physician confesses that he indeed is the one responsible for the murders.
He shoots at the detective with what turn out to be blank cartridges.
When the other physician emerges from the crypt, the inspector and the doctor are there waiting to arrest him.

Explaining the meaning of the document found in the crypt to the sister, the detective suggests that the other physician had discovered an old land grant that entitled the family to a fortune of millions of pounds, and had hatched a deadly scheme to gain it for himself.
The devious doctor had killed both brothers, making the sister heir to the money, and then sought to claim her as his bride by framing her sweetheart, the captain, for the slayings.
Learning of this, the sister destroys the document that would have made her rich, not wanting to profit at the cost of others' lives.
Driving away with the doctor, the detective muses on the sister's selfless act, "There's a new spirit abroad in the land.
The old days of grab and greed are on their way out.
We're beginning to think of what we owe the other fellow, not just what we're compelled to give him.

The time's coming, doctor, when we shan't be able to fill our bellies in comfort while other folk go hungry, or sleep in warm beds while others shiver in the cold; when we shan't be able to kneel and thank God for blessings before our shining altars while men anywhere are kneeling in either physical or spiritual subjection....
And God willing, we'll live to see that day, doctor."
The convict, a prisoner serving a lengthy sentence on a remote group of islands cuts a deal with two army officers, the major and the captain, in command of the prison.
He reveals the location of a stash of loot in exchange for their help in helping him to escape from jail.
The proceeds are to be split equally between the three of them.
The major and the captain go to investigate the treasure which is hidden in an old Indian fortress.
When they unearth the valuable trinkets behind a brick wall it sparks a violent quarrel between the two men with each wanting to take all of the treasure.
After a struggle the major kills his accomplice and returns to his home country without fulfilling his pledge to help the convict escape.
A number of years later the major is now living in the capital in great wealth thanks to his theft of the treasure.
However, he is disturbed to read of the escape from jail of the convict.
He becomes haunted by the sound of the convict's wooden leg and is convinced he will shortly be killed in revenge for his past betrayal of the convict.
He calls his sons, the first son and the second son, to him and tells them of his murky past that had gained him the wealth on which the family fortune is built.
He reveals that the captain had a daughter and instructs his sons to send her a valuable necklace and split their inheritance with her.
Shortly afterwards the major is murdered before he can reveal the location of the bulk of his treasure.
The killing has been committed by the convict who has broken out of jail with two accomplices, a heavily-tattooed convict and a native.
He reveals himself and menaces the second son into telling him about the captain's daughter.
The gang soon begin threatening the captain's daughter in the hope that she will hand over her share of the treasure to them.
Frightened, she calls in the detective to help her protect herself.

She is approached by the second son, who reveals that the secret hiding place of the treasure has been discovered, and offers her the share as instructed by his father, and takes them to the family house.
However, when they arrive there the first son is dead, and the treasure is missing.
The detective has his theory about the murder, but the innocent second son is arrested for murder by the incompent detective from the police force.
The detective and the doctor set out to prove the second son's innocence and track down the gang who are threatening the captain's daughter.
They soon discover that the convict and his accomplices are waiting to take the necklace from the captain's daughter to complete their haul and then flee the country and are hiding out in a circus.
The doctor unwisely takes the captain's daughter to investigate, and she is forcibly taken by them.
The convict's gang plan to make their escape by boat up the river, but they are pursued by the detective and the doctor.
The film climaxes in a shoot-out at a deserted warehouse.
The film begins on the physician's estate with gypsies camping on the grounds.
Inside the mansion, the victim screams in her bedroom and then collapses in the hallway.
She is discovered by her sister, the heiress.
The victim's dying words are "the band, speckled."
She then dies and their stepfather, the physician, arrives.
Soon there is an inquest into the mysterious death, and the physician plots with the housekeeper and his Indian servant, the attendant.
The doctor attends the inquest as an old friend of the sisters' family in the colony.
He acts protectively to the heiress and advises her to consult the detective if she ever feels in danger.
At the detective's lodgings later, the doctor summarises the inquest to the detective, describing the various witnesses and evidence.
The detective files it away in his system—he operates a modern office with female secretaries and a voice recording device.
One year later, the heiress is engaged, and her fiancé must leave for a plantation in the distant city for a year.
The heiress is afraid and suggests that they marry sooner, so that she may go with him to the distant city.
The physician is upset by these plans and decides to murder her to prevent the loss of her inheritance.
The physician forces the heiress to move from her room into the victim's old room.
The next day, the heiress meets with the detective and the doctor in the detective's lodgings they describe her case.
Her sister the victim had been engaged to be married before she dies, and the heiress remembers hearing mysterious music that night.
Now the heiress is engaged and is also hearing the mysterious music again.
The detective questions her and sends her out of the room through a separate entrance when her stepfather arrives.
The physician barges in and threatens the detective, but he is not deterred.
In the afternoon, the doctor arrives alone to visit the heiress while her stepfather is not home.
The detective is in disguise as a workman dealing with the repairs to the building.
Together they investigate the physician's room and discover several clues, such as a bowl of milk, a dog whip, and a mirror.
Next, they investigate the victim's room, which has a bell-rope that doesn't ring and a ventilator near the bed.
The ventilator opens into the physician's room but is hidden by a painting.
When the physician returns, the detective and the doctor temporarily leave the heiress at the house but plan to sneak into the room later to investigate.
That night, the heiress spends the night within the victim's room while the detective and the doctor secretly keep watch with her.
After snake-charming music plays, a snake enters the room through the ventilator, and the detective attacks it, sending it back to the physician's room.
The detective, the doctor, and the heiress enter his room and discover the physician dead from a snake bite.
The detective forces the attendant, the servant, to charm the snake so they can put it in the safe.
The victim's last words about a "speckled band" were in fact describing "a swamp adder, the deadliest snake in the colony".
The venomous snake had been sent to the victim's room by the physician to murder her for her inheritance.
The physician had intended to do the same to the heiress.
The movie ends with the detective conducting an experiment in the detective's lodgings.
The doctor arrives dressed for a wedding, and the detective therefore deduces that he is going to a wedding.
The doctor is pleased to tell the detective that he is wrong, that he has just come from the wedding of the heiress and her groom.
The detective offers his "condolences" rather than congratulations.
The doctor says in amusement that "we all come to it", meaning marriage.
After the doctor leaves, the detective disagrees quietly, "Not all, my dear doctor... not all".

The consulting detective fakes his own death in the northern country in order to investigate a number of bizarre apparent suicides that he is convinced are part of an elaborate plot by "a female master criminal".

Returning to his assistant the doctor in secret, the detective notes that all the victims were wealthy gamblers, so disguised as "an alias", a distinguished Indian officer, he stalks the city's gaming clubs.
It is not long before he encounters the archvillain, the mastermind.
The detective discovers that she seeks out men short of money, persuades them to pawn their life insurance policies with her accomplices, then kills them.
The detective sets himself up as her next victim, discovering that she uses the deadly spider, a rare species, whose venom causes such excruciating pain that the victims kill themselves.
The detective also finds the footprint of a child nearby.
Searching for evidence the detective and the doctor visit eminent arachnologist the scientist, who may have supplied the deadly creatures.
The detective soon realizes that the man he is speaking to is an impostor, but the man makes his escape.
Searching the premises, the detective finds the corpse of the real scientist, as well as his journals, which allude to something or someone from a distant region immune to the spider venom.
This baffles the detective until he finds the model skeleton of a child.

However, the doctor points out that the relation of the skull and the circumference of the chest prove it is not a child, and the detective deduces that the foreign thing described in the journal is a pygmy.
The detective and the doctor continue their investigations at a nearby fairground, where the detective allows himself to fall into the clutches of the mastermind and her gang.
Bound and gagged, the detective is tied behind a moving target in a shooting gallery, at which the inspector and the doctor take pot shots with a.22 rifle.
However the detective manages to escape, and the inspector and the police arrest the mastermind, her gang, and the pygmy.
As an indication of respect for her intellect, the detective tells the inspector to spare the mastermind the indignity of handcuffs, saying "she'll go quietly."
The mastermind appreciatively smiles and thanks the detective as she is taken away.
The film opens in the city in the present day.
The body of the first victim is found dead on a train, apparently by suicide, but in fact, murdered.
A secret society holds a meeting in the dockside district, chaired by lawyer the chairman.
He reports the first victim's death, which follows the recent death of fellow member the colonel, whose daughter the young woman inherits her father's membership.
The chairman explains that the first victim's financial interest in the society will be divided between the surviving members, with the first victim's widow getting nothing.
The first victim's widow visits the detective at the detective's lodgings to ask his help to get payment from the chairman.
The first victim's widow shows the detective a couplet from the counting-out rhyme "a nursery rhyme" written in pencil on a scrap of paper, which her husband had received before his death.
Such couplets, counting down, are delivered before each of the subsequent murders.
The detective tells the doctor that the chairman is the city's most dangerous crook and has eluded him several times previously, but this time he intends to catch him.
The detective notes an advertisement in code in the newspaper which he believes is connected with the case.
The chairman warns the young woman that she should not marry her fiancé the young man for the time being.
While they are talking one of the society's members, the captain, rushes in and the young woman sees him killed by a shot fired through the window.
She is then terrified by the murderer's apparent accomplice and faints.
The captain's body is identified by his wife, whose lawyer is the chairman.
The detective does not believe what she tells him.
It appears that the members of the society are being killed off.
The inspector, the detective and the doctor investigate the death of member another victim.
The detective and the doctor visit the chairman to ask about the first victim's money, without success.
They pass the captain's wife, who is arriving.
The detective explains to the doctor that the key to the code can be found in a well-known almanac, which he has observed on the chairman's desk.
The chairman pays a call to the young woman to invite her to another meeting of the society, the syndicate.
The young woman tells the young man that her late father had told her that the chairman would arrange for her to receive a large inheritance.
The young man visits the detective, who says the young woman is in great danger.
The detective disguises himself and goes to the captain's family mansion the country house in a seaside town (spelled slightly differently), which is now for sale by the captain's wife.
His investigations there make him suspicious that the captain's wife is collaborating with the chairman.
The detective places newspaper advertisements requesting any information about the syndicate.
The syndicate holds another meeting, where some of its remaining members, especially the nervous member, are fearful for their lives.
The chairman tells them that, after waiting five years, their scheme is about to pay out one million pounds, which is £200,000 for each of the five remaining members.
The detective and the young man arrive as the meeting breaks up.
They smell gas and are just in time to save the young woman, who had been left to die.
The terrified nervous member goes to the detective to get his help after an apparent attempt is made on his life.
The nervous member and the young woman are lured to the country house without realizing they are next to be killed.
The detective, the inspector and police officers surround and enter the mansion and rescue them.
The killer is revealed as the captain, whose death had been fabricated.
He is arrested for three murders, and the captain's wife is arrested as an accomplice.
The chairman arrives with the gems, and is arrested as an accomplice.
The young woman and the young man depart happily, and the detective is content he has rid the city of another master criminal.
In the city, the young woman verifies that a carpenter has completed a coffin for her recently deceased mother's body, which she is transporting to the northern country by train.

She boards the train that evening, as do the noblewoman, who owns and is transporting the famous priceless diamond; the noblewoman's son, the young nobleman; the detective, whom the young nobleman has hired to protect the diamond; the inspector, who is also worried about the diamond's safety; and the doctor and the doctor's friend the major.
The detective briefly examines the diamond.
Shortly afterward, the young nobleman is murdered and the diamond is stolen.
The inspector, the detective, and the doctor learn nothing conclusive in questioning the other passengers.
At one point during the investigation, the doctor believes an elderly couple is guilty of the crime but the only crime that they have committed is stealing a teapot from a hotel.

While searching the train, the detective is pushed out of the train, nearly to his death, but climbs back into the day coach and discovers a secret compartment in the coffin carrying the young woman's mother.
He suspects that one of the people on the train is the notorious jewel thief the colonel.
Upon further questioning, the young woman admits that a man paid her to transport the coffin.
As the doctor and the major join the group, the detective reveals that he swapped the diamond with an imitation while examining it.
The inspector ostensibly takes possession of the real diamond.
In the luggage compartment, the detective and the doctor find a train guard murdered with a poisoned dart.
Meanwhile, a street criminal named the accomplice incapacitates the conductor.
The accomplice was hidden inside the coffin, and is in cahoots with the major, who is, in fact, the colonel.

The accomplice and the colonel go to the inspector's room, where the accomplice knocks the inspector unconscious and steals the diamond from him; but the colonel double-crosses the accomplice, shooting him dead with the same dart gun he used to kill the young nobleman and the guard.
The train makes an unexpected stop to pick up several Scottish policemen, led allegedly by the second inspector.

The detective informs the second inspector that the major is really the colonel, and the second inspector arrests the colonel and finds the diamond in his vest, but the colonel seizes a policeman's gun and pulls the emergency cord to stop the train.
During a scuffle in which the lights are turned off, the detective subdues and handcuffs the colonel, then secretly hides him under a table.
When the lights are turned on again, the officers leave the train with the inspector, his coat covering his face, believing he is the colonel.

As the train departs, the inspector captures the thieves in the railway station, and the detective reveals to the doctor and the colonel that he recognized the second inspector as an impostor and recovered the diamond from him during the fight.
When several women are murdered and their forefingers severed, the detective and the doctor are called into action by the inspector, but the detective is baffled by the crimes at the start.
Wealthy widower the baronet has a romantic evening with the glamorous young woman, which adjourns to her apartment.

After drinking a "special cocktail" mixed by the young woman's maid and becoming entranced by a bowl of floating flowers on her coffee table, he awakes ten hours later in a stupor at a flop house in a seedy part of the city.
Hearing a news crier hawking papers blaring a new mutilation murder, he cringes when he finds a woman's forefinger in his pocket.
The next day his daughter comes to the detective and the doctor (unaware that the master criminal's henchman is following her).
She tells the detective and the doctor that she saw her father burying something in their garden the previous night.
Later, she dug up a box containing a forefinger and shows it to them.
The baronet is then found dead in his home, obviously murdered to keep him from talking.
The detective theorizes that the master criminal, who was supposed to have been hanged in a foreign city, is alive and responsible for the crimes.
The doctor is called to attend to a medical emergency.
Minutes later, the master criminal appears and explains that he faked the doctor's call so he could talk to the detective.
The master criminal leaves, and the doctor returns.
The detective describes what had transpired, notices that a previously shut window shade in the empty house across the street is now open, and sends the doctor to investigate.
There the doctor believes that he sees a man with a rifle shoot the detective in his apartment through the open window.
The detective then arrives and explains that he put a plaster bust in his place as a target.
The inspector takes the shooter, a hypnotized ex-army sniper, away, but the man is kidnapped and later killed and left on the detective's doorstep.
The detective has surmised that blackmail is the game, and is now convinced that the master criminal is having women killed, and their forefingers cut off as the "hook" to a blackmail scheme.
He then has rich marks hypnotized, who awaken surrounded by clues convincing them they have committed the murders.
The crimes are so heinous that even though a victim may discover he is innocent, he will still remain silent to avoid having his name besmirched through association.
The detective befriends the young woman at the hypnotism club, a magicians' society, suspecting that she is in cahoots with the master criminal.
He's taken to her house to be hypnotized, but she asserts he is too anxious to be put under, and insists he take a pill containing a rare narcotic.
The master criminal enters and has one of his men prick the detective with a knife to confirm that he is hypnotized.
He then has the detective write a suicide note, then walk out onto the upper story ledge of the young woman's apartment, where he will be commanded to jump to his death.
The doctor and the police arrive in the nick of time.
The detective then reveals he had foiled the master criminal's plan by secretly ingesting a drug that rendered him insensitive to pain, allowing him to fake hypnosis.
The master criminal then wrests free from a policemen and leaps to the ledge of a neighboring building.
However, he slams hard into a metal drain pipe, dazing him, which comes free and causes him to plummet to his death.
After a lustful landlord in the remote village rapes a young girl, she kills herself.
Thereafter, the landlord is killed by what the local people call the girl's vengeful spirit.
Then the landlord's son is also reportedly killed by the same spirit.
Twenty years after the landlord's death, his grandson the heir comes to the village and is warned by the locals that the spirit will kill him as well, but he does not believe them.
He hears the singing voice of the supposed spirit the first night from the swamp.
The next day as he wakes up, he finds out about the village girl, a carefree girl who is the niece of an old man, the elder.
The singing continues the second night, but the heir is unable to find the identity of the girl singing the song.
He notices that there is a source of light in his house on the terrace.
The next day, the heir finds that his coat is lost.
The news reaches the village girl that the heir has been killed.
The village girl does not believe this and runs into the forest, and the heir appears before her.
He says it was not he that was killed, but another man wearing his suit.
He was killed in the swamp under the same tree where his father and grandfather were killed.
Later that night, the heir sees the manservant, his servant, arguing with a girl.
When he inquires, the manservant explains that the man who was killed under the tree was none other than his sister's husband.

The manservant used to give a signal from the roof (terrace) of the house occasionally to his fugitive brother-in-law, using the light from his lantern, after which that man would come to the house for supplies.
Since the fugitive needed a coat, the manservant stole the heir's coat and gave it to him.
Obviously, the "spirit" had chanced upon the fugitive in the forest, mistaken him for the heir, and killed him.
The village girl strongly urges the heir to leave the village and go back to town, since a person wearing his coat was killed by the spirit, but the heir refuses to leave.
The elder forbids his niece the village girl to meet the heir, since tongues in the village have begun to wag.
Also, says the elder, the heir is the grandson of a rapist and two generations of his family have met violent deaths; the heir himself has been marked by the spirit.
Why get involved with him?
The village girl is deeply saddened after this conversation with her uncle.
Seeing the village girl so downcast, the elder tells her to call the heir near the swamp where they will talk, and he will convince the heir to leave the village.
The heir goes to the swamp, and the spirit tries to kill him, but he escapes.
The village girl finds out that the one who was pretending to be the spirit of the girl was none other than her uncle the elder.
It was the elder's daughter who had been raped by the landlord, so he killed the landlord and the landlord's son and was trying to kill the landlord's grandson.
Police arrive and persuade the elder to surrender himself.
The heir and the village girl meet each other and have a happy ending.
